name: 24LC04BT-I_SN
title: 24AA04, 24LC04B, 24FC04: 4-Kbit I2C serial EEPROM
summary: A 4 Kbit serial EEPROM, two 256-byte blocks behind a two-wire I2C-compatible interface, with a 16-byte page buffer, self-timed 5 ms writes and a pin that write-protects the whole array. Three grades: the 24AA04 runs from 1.7 V at up to 400 kHz, the 24LC04B from 2.5 V at 400 kHz, and the 24FC04 from 1.7 V at 1 MHz. Address pins A0, A1 and A2 have no internal connection. 24LC04BT-I/SN is the 24LC04B in the 8-lead SOIC, industrial range, on tape and reel.
key_figures: 24AA04 and 24FC04 1.7 V to 5.5 V; 24LC04B 2.5 V to 5.5 V

The CSP package code is CS16K, where 16K stands for 160K process technology.

operation.text: 4 Kbit of EEPROM arranged as two blocks of 256 bytes, reached over a two-wire I2C-compatible bus. Writes go through a 16-byte page buffer and are timed on chip, finishing in 5 ms at most. A0, A1 and A2 have no internal connection.
The device is always a slave. The master drives SCL, owns the bus and issues every Start and Stop; either side may send or receive, as the master decides.

Idle: SDA and SCL both high. A transfer may begin only on an idle bus. Start: SDA falls while SCL is high; every command opens with one. Stop: SDA rises while SCL is high; every operation closes with one. Data: SDA may change only while SCL is low and is read while SCL is high, one bit per clock.

After each byte the receiver pulls SDA low through the ninth clock's high period; the master supplies that extra clock. The device gives no acknowledge while an internal write is running. When reading, the master ends the transfer by leaving the last byte unacknowledged, after which the device releases SDA high so the master can issue a Stop.

The first byte after a Start is the control byte: control code 1010, two ignored bits, block bit B0, then R/W (1 read, 0 write). B0 is the top bit of the 9-bit memory address and picks one of the two 256-byte blocks. The device acknowledges a matching slave address; the next byte in a write is the 8-bit word address within the block.
Start, control byte with R/W = 0, word address, one data byte, each acknowledged by the device, then Stop. The Stop starts the internal write cycle; during it the device does not acknowledge.

As a byte write, but the master sends up to 16 data bytes before the Stop. Each byte advances the low four address bits; the upper four bits and B0 stay fixed. Bytes wait in a 16-byte buffer and are written after the Stop. More than 16 bytes wrap the counter and overwrite the earliest; only the final 16 are kept. A page starts at a multiple of 16, and a write that runs past a page boundary wraps to the start of that same page.
WP at VCC blocks writes to the entire array (000-1FF); WP at VSS allows them. Reads are unaffected. WP must be tied to one or the other. The CSP has no WP and no hardware write protection.

Since the device ignores its address while writing, the master can find the end of a write cycle by repeatedly sending Start and a write control byte (R/W = 0) right after the Stop. No acknowledge means still busy; an acknowledge means the cycle is done and the next read or write can follow.

An internal address pointer holds the last address accessed plus one. Start and a control byte with R/W = 1 make the device acknowledge and send the byte at that pointer; the master does not acknowledge and sends Stop.

The master first loads the address by starting a write: control byte with R/W = 0, then the word address. Instead of data it then sends a new Start and the control byte with R/W = 1; the device sends the addressed byte, the master leaves it unacknowledged and sends Stop.

Begun like a current-address or random read; the master acknowledges each byte and the device sends the next address in turn. The pointer advances after every byte, so the whole memory can be read in one operation. The master ends it with no acknowledge and a Stop.
SCL and SDA have Schmitt-trigger inputs and spike filters (50 ns max suppressed spike width); the output has slope control against ground bounce.
SDA is open drain and needs a pull-up to VCC: typically 10 kΩ at 100 kHz and 2 kΩ at 400 kHz and 1 MHz.

Endurance above 1 million erase/write cycles; retention beyond 200 years, ESD protection over 4,000 V. Standby current 1 µA max (I-temp) and read current 1 mA max. AEC-Q100 qualified. RoHS compliant. Factory programming is offered.
